docs.title: Generative AI Project Template
docs.text: A FastAPI backend and NiceGUI frontend for chat, with local Ollama or cloud models through LiteLLM. Includes uv workspace tooling, tests, Docker Compose and GitHub releases.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
Requires Make, Bash, Git and uv. uv provisions Python 3.14.8.

git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git
cd generative-ai-project-template
make install-dev
cp .env.example .env

Configure INFERENCE_* and EMBEDDINGS_* in .env for your model provider, then start the app:

make run

Open the frontend at http://localhost:8080 or backend API docs at http://localhost:8000/docs. For local Ollama, install it with make install-ollama, then use make run-with-ollama to prepare the models and start both services.

docs.title: Other ways to run
docs.text:
Command Use make docker-compose Backend, frontend and Ollama in containers; Compose 2.24+ make docker-compose-cuda Same stack with GPU access for Ollama; NVIDIA drivers required make docker-compose-rebuild Rebuild containers after source changes make run-backend / make run-frontend Start either application separately

Python PyTorch extras are optional for model development; Ollama inference runs outside Python. See Setup for provider URLs, CUDA variants and timeouts.

docs.title: Develop
docs.text:
make install-dev installs the Git hooks in a checkout; make pre-commit-install reinstalls them. For offline work, run make test-local; before a PR, configure the integration services and run make check. That includes live LLM/Ollama/API tests; Testing lists the requirements. make help lists all targets.

Task Guide Install, run or configure providers Setup Add routes, settings or dependencies Project structure Prepare a contribution Contributing and conventions Run tests Testing Publish or retry a release Release Start your own project Use this template and rename guide

Preview documentation with make deploy-doc-local.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the contributors of this repository, who are responsible for enforcement, by opening an issue. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Follow Setup, pick an issue and wait to be assigned.
  2. Branch from dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>.
  3. Update the relevant docs, configure the integration services and run make check (Testing). It includes real model requests.
  4. Open a PR to dev using a Conventional Commit title. PRs are squash-merged; the title determines the version.

CI provisions its own Ollama service and runs the same software suites; inspect its result after pushing. See Release for publication and recovery. Coding agents need explicit approval for commits, pushes and publishing. Follow the Code of Conduct; report security issues through SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take security issues seriously. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose your findings and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

Please do NOT open a public issue or pull request for security vulnerabilities.

To report a security vulnerability privately, use GitHub private vulnerability reporting (preferred):

  • https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template/security/advisories/new

For any other question, open an issue to reach the contributors of this repository, but never include vulnerability details in a public issue.

When reporting, please include as much of the following as possible:

  • A description of the vulnerability and its impact
  • The affected component(s) and version(s)
  • Steps to reproduce the issue
  • Any suggested remediation (if known)

You should receive a response within 48 hours. If you do not, please follow up on the same channel.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are only provided for the latest released version. Please always use the latest version available.

docs.title: Disclosure Policy
docs.text:
• You will receive an acknowledgment of your report within 48 hours.
  • We will investigate the issue and determine its impact and severity.
  • We will fix the issue in a future release and credit you if you wish to be credited.
  • We ask that you do not publicly disclose the vulnerability until we have published a fix and given users time to update.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep everything up to date.
  • Do not expose admin interfaces directly to the internet without a reverse proxy and proper authentication.
  • Use strong, unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text: Install the workspace and run it with your chosen model provider.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Make, Bash, Git and uv on Ubuntu 22.04+ or macOS. uv provisions Python 3.14.8 (>=3.14.8,<3.15); run make install-uv if uv is missing. Docker/Compose 2.24+ is optional; GPU Compose requires NVIDIA drivers.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git
cd generative-ai-project-template
make install-dev
cp .env.example .env

This installs backend, frontend and dev/docs tools, without PyTorch, and, in a Git checkout, the Git hooks. Configure INFERENCE_* and EMBEDDINGS_* in .env using your provider's LiteLLM model names.

For full checks, configure the integration prerequisites, then run:

make pre-commit   # static checks and hooks
make test-all     # tests, including real model requests
make docs-build   # strict documentation build

make check runs all three at once (and first warns if the Git hooks are missing). Use make test-local for offline diagnostics.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
For a cloud provider, remote Ollama or an already managed model server:

make run

For local Ollama:

make install-ollama
make run-with-ollama

The local command starts/reuses Ollama and downloads missing models before starting the app. Keep OLLAMA_MODEL_NAME and OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME consistent with the .env deployment names.

URL / command Use http://localhost:8080 Frontend http://localhost:8000/docs Backend API docs make run-backend / make run-frontend Start either side separately make run-frontend-backend Start both without provider preparation

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
make docker-compose

Use make docker-compose-cuda for NVIDIA GPU access. After source changes, run make docker-compose-rebuild or make docker-compose-cuda-rebuild. For bundled Ollama, .env provider URLs must use http://ollama:11434; native execution uses http://localhost:11434. Preflight checks URLs and Docker access without rewriting them. Wait for model provisioning and backend readiness. Direct docker compose up bypasses preflight.

Models persist in ollama-data; missing models are downloaded on first start. Container logs default to INFO; LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG enables reload.

docs.title: Timeouts and retries
docs.text:
Override these values in .env or the environment, then restart the app. Keep the model timeout below the chat deadline and the frontend timeout above it. The chat deadline includes retries; HTTPX timeouts apply per network operation.

Setting Default Controls INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 One model request INFERENCE_RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS 2 Delay between rate-limit attempts; zero allowed INFERENCE_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 Total rate-limit attempts CHAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 90 Chat deadline, including retries BACKEND_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 120 Frontend HTTP read/write/pool timeout BACKEND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 5 Frontend connection timeout

Timeouts must be positive and attempts at least one. Compose forwards all six settings.

docs.text:

For publication, see release credentials.

docs.title: Editor and agent rules
docs.text:
Select .venv/bin/python; mark backend/src, frontend/src and tests as source/test roots. Follow .editorconfig for formatting. Agent rules live in AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md links to it for Claude Code. Edit AGENTS.md to update the shared instructions.

make help lists all targets. Next: Conventions and Testing.

docs.title: 2. Project structure
docs.text: Where things are, and where to add yours.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
A uv workspace with two packages that share one version and one git tag.

pyproject.toml          workspace root: shared dev/docs tools, ruff, pytest, semantic-release, commitizen
backend/                package genai-template-backend (FastAPI)
  pyproject.toml        backend dependencies (optional cpu / cuda PyTorch extras)
  src/genai_template_backend/
    app.py              FastAPI application
    api/llm.py          LLM client (LiteLLM)
    api/routes/chat.py  chat routes
    backend_settings.py settings (pydantic-settings, .env) and the loguru logger
frontend/               package genai-template-frontend (NiceGUI)
  src/genai_template_frontend/
    main.py             NiceGUI application
    components/chat.py  chat component
    frontend_settings.py
tests/unit/             self-contained backend, frontend and tooling tests
tests/integration/      real LLM, Ollama and API-to-model tests
tests/hardware/         explicit CUDA checks
scripts/                commit parser, release artifact checks and workspace docs generators
makefiles/              one .mk per concern, included by Makefile
docs/developer/         this guide
docker-compose.yml      application services and model provisioning
docker-compose-cuda.yml GPU override for Ollama
Dockerfile              backend and frontend image targets
.github/                workflows, composite actions, Renovate, issue and PR templates
properdocs.yml          documentation site (MkDocs Material)
CHANGELOG.md            written by semantic-release, never by hand

docs.title: Where to add things
docs.text: Task Where Help a backend route backend/src/genai_template_backend/api/routes/ Add a backend route a setting backend_settings.py or frontend_settings.py Add a setting a dependency uv add --package <package> <pkg> Add a dependency a make target makefiles/<concern>.mk with a ## description —

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
1. Add a field to the ApplicationSettings class in backend_settings.py (or frontend_settings.py). A secret is a SecretStr.
  2. Add it, with a safe example value, to .env.example.
  3. Read it through the module-level settings object.

docs.title: Add a backend route
docs.text:
1. Add the route in backend/src/genai_template_backend/api/routes/ (an APIRouter).
  2. Include the router in app.py.
  3. Add isolated API tests in tests/unit/backend/ and live-service tests in tests/integration/. The route appears in /docs automatically.

docs.title: Add a dependency
docs.text: uv add --package genai-template-backend <pkg> (or --package genai-template-frontend), then commit uv.lock.

docs.title: 3. Conventions
docs.text: The rules every change follows.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Use the make targets (make help): CI runs the same ones.
  • Docstrings on public functions and classes (Google style): they generate the API reference.
  • Settings come from backend_settings.py / frontend_settings.py (pydantic-settings, .env), never os.environ scattered in the code. Secrets are SecretStr.

  • Logging with the package's loguru logger, not print:

    from genai_template_backend.backend_settings import logger

logger.info("Loaded {} items", count)

  • Log, then raise; do not swallow exceptions:

    if not path.exists():
    logger.error(f"File not found: {path}. Current directory: {Path.cwd()}")
    raise FileNotFoundError(path)

    In an except block, logger.exception(...) logs the message and the stack trace. Not raising is fine only when a loop must go on after one failure.

  • Large data: Polars. CPU-bound work: multiprocessing pool map. I/O-bound work: asyncio.

docs.title: Branches and pull requests
docs.text:
1. Comment on (or create) the issue and wait to be assigned.
  2. Branch off dev: feature/<name> or bugfix/<name>. Stay up to date with git merge dev (branch already pushed) or git rebase dev (local only).
  3. Run make check (4. Testing), then open a pull request to dev. Its title follows the commit convention below: it becomes the squash commit and decides the version.
  4. When dev is ready, a pull request dev → main releases it.
  5. After a release, merge main back into dev (merge commit, direct push). On conflicts on CHANGELOG.md or a pyproject.toml version, keep main's and regenerate uv.lock with uv lock.
Merge Strategy Why feature/* → dev squash one conventional commit per feature dev → main squash one commit for semantic-release to evaluate main → dev (sync) merge commit, direct push syncs stable metadata; [skip ci] in the release commit prevents a spurious RC

Never edit a version in pyproject.toml or create a tag by hand: semantic-release does both.

docs.title: Commit convention
docs.text:
[emoji] <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>, the emoji is optional (Gitmoji).

Emoji Type Aliases Release 🐛 fix bugfix, hotfix patch ⚡️ perf patch ✨ feat feature minor 💥 feat! BREAKING CHANGE: footer major ♻️ 📝 🎨 🧪 🔧 👷 📦 refactor, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build none

A ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer makes any allowed type a breaking change (major release).

✨ feat(auth): add GitHub App token rotation
🐛 fix(llm): handle empty response from the API
💥 feat!(api): remove the v1 endpoint

feat(auth): redesign token flow

BREAKING CHANGE: /v1/token removed, use /v2/auth instead

On dev, a releasable commit increments the release-candidate counter (1.1.0-rc.1 → 1.1.0-rc.2) unless a larger bump is needed (for example, a breaking change → 2.0.0-rc.1 when the last stable release was 1.0.0).

Scopes are optional. Common scopes: llm, api, frontend, backend, ci, deps. The commit message is checked on commit (commitizen) and the pull request title by ci.yml.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never write a credential to a file of the repository, even untracked: use environment variables or .env (git-ignored).
  • detect-secrets runs on commit. For a line that intentionally references a secret placeholder (${{ secrets.X }}), add # pragma: allowlist secret. File-level exclusions in .pre-commit-config.yaml only for recurring false positives; never exclude a whole workflow to silence one line.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Adding, renaming or removing one, in the same change: the setting in backend_settings.py or frontend_settings.py, .env.example, and the workflow env: if CI needs it.

docs.title: Dependencies (Renovate)
docs.text:
Renovate (.github/renovate.json5) opens pull requests with the renovate and dependencies labels; most routine updates have a 7-day cooldown; security fixes are not grouped and open at once. Renovate pins runtime dependencies, including existing ranges; uv.lock makes builds reproducible. Review every Renovate pull request; a dependency dashboard issue lists the pending ones.

  1. CI runs make test-all on Python 3.14.8 only.
  2. Renovate widens the Python range only after dependency dashboard approval, in one python runtime pull request with the Docker base image. Review the interpreter before merging. The exact CI Python (UV_PYTHON in the quality workflow), the README and this document are not tracked: update them by hand in that pull request.
  3. PyPI updates use strict Python compatibility filtering. Weekly lockfile maintenance refreshes versions already permitted by dependency ranges; review the lockfile and CI results too.
  4. Renovate updates dependency files, GitHub Actions and pre-commit revisions; update README and developer documentation when the supported Python range changes. Docs are not rewritten automatically.
  5. Renovate tracks the Node pin used by pre-commit. Stable updates wait seven days and use chore; major upgrades open as normal pull requests labelled needs-compatibility-review.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text: Run offline tests during development and real model integration before a pull request.

docs.title: Before a pull request
docs.text:
Complete setup, then run the three checks:

make pre-commit   # static checks and hooks
make test-all     # tests, including real model requests
make docs-build   # strict documentation build

make check runs all three at once (and first warns if the Git hooks are missing):

make check

test-all runs the unit/NiceGUI component tests, then live LLM, Ollama and API-to-model tests.

The full integration gate requires INFERENCE_* configured for a running Ollama service with the selected model installed, including when you normally use a cloud provider. Workers do not download models. Missing services, failed cleanup, empty runs, skipped or deselected integration cases fail the gate. Report unavailable integration as incomplete; collection or offline tests do not replace it.

docs.title: Focused checks
docs.text:
Command Scope / requirement make check pre-commit-status, pre-commit, test-all and docs-build make test-local Offline unit and NiceGUI component/page simulations make test-unit Settings, logic and tooling tests make test-component NiceGUI simulations without a browser or real backend make test-all Every software suite, including live integration make test-integration-check Credential-free collection; no endpoint probes make test-integration Real LLM, Ollama and API tests make test-integration-llm / make test-integration-ollama Selected live provider suites make test-smoke-ollama Bounded model warmup/connectivity request make test-hardware-cuda GPU check; optional CUDA PyTorch install required make pre-commit Static hooks and strict docs; FILES="path/a path/b" selects files make pre-commit-status Warn when the Git hooks are not installed make docs-build Strict docs build only make build-package Verify the backend/frontend wheel and sdist sets

Tests use N=4 workers by default; reduce N for rate limits or use N=0 for serial diagnostics. Focused targets accept ARGS filters; test-all rejects them. Plain pytest selects offline suites. Coverage instrumentation is not configured; UI simulations and synthetic artifacts do not prove a browser, container or installed wheel works.

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text:
Folder Tests tests/unit/backend/ Settings, LLM logic, isolated API checks tests/unit/frontend/ NiceGUI components/pages tests/unit/tooling/ Release, docs, startup and test helpers tests/integration/ Live LLM/Ollama/API tests and fixtures tests/hardware/ Explicit GPU checks

Keep live/UI fixtures scoped to their folders. Offline tests use synthetic settings; endpoint probes run in integration fixtures, never at collection. Parallel tests share no state. Live generation uses short prompts, a 64-token output limit and no optional Ollama reasoning. Release tooling tests use isolated command substitutes and never publish.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: CI and release workflows run test-all on Python 3.14.8 with a dedicated runner-local Ollama service. INTEGRATION_OLLAMA_MODEL overrides the default qwen3.5:0.8b. CI provisions the model, warms it with test-smoke-ollama, then tests with explicit local settings, no cloud credentials, INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=180 and CHAT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=240 for queued CPU requests. The service is stopped after testing; logs and reports/integration.json / integration.xml are included in integration-results. Summaries report failures even when setup prevents execution.

docs.title: Static and documentation hooks
docs.text:
Hooks check formatting and lint (Ruff), syntax and whitespace, secrets, Markdown and spelling, the lockfile and the strict docs build, workflow syntax (actionlint) and workflow security (zizmor). Commitizen runs only at the commit-msg stage. make install-dev installs the Git hooks in a checkout (not in CI or Docker); run make pre-commit-install if that step failed, and make pre-commit-status (part of make check) warns when they are missing. make pre-commit only runs the hooks and never installs them. See .pre-commit-config.yaml for the full list; pip-audit, bandit and markdown-link-check are disabled. .github/zizmor.yml holds the one zizmor exception: the release workflow's checkouts keep their credentials because they push.

Image, Compose and runtime checks remain separate from software validation.

docs.title: 5. Release
docs.text: Publish Python packages to GitHub Releases and documentation to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Automatic release
docs.text: Merge a releasable change to dev for a release candidate, or promote dev to main for a stable release. release.yml validates the source, versions and builds every package, then uploads artifacts. A tagged stable release also deploys docs from that tag. Docs-only commits do not publish docs. Versions come from Conventional Commits; never edit versions or create tags manually.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
Use a clean main (stable) or dev (prerelease), synchronized with origin. Complete setup and GitHub login, then run:

make check
make release

The release command versions, builds and uploads the full wheel/sdist set. It changes Git and GitHub; coding agents need explicit per-action approval. Local publication also asks you to type yes. For a stable manual release, publish docs separately from the clean released tag:

make deploy-doc-gh

That command pushes gh-pages and requires separate authorization.

docs.title: Retry an interrupted release
docs.text:
Retry the failed CI job if its tested source still matches the release. Locally, rerun make release on the matching clean release branch. To upload from a clean checkout of the exact release tag:

make build-package
make release-assets

If newer application commits exist, let their own workflow validate/release them. Never rebuild an older release from later source. release-assets can create a missing GitHub release and replaces same-named attachments (--clobber); it does not publish to a package index.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
gh auth login

Credentials resolve from GH_TOKEN (environment or local .env), then the token saved by gh auth login, then a hidden terminal prompt. release-assets uses the token or gh login. CI supplies its automatic GitHub token; never print credentials. A tooling-only environment can use make install-release; docs need make install-tools or make install-dev.

docs.title: Release sequence and safeguards
docs.text:
Target / stage Behavior make release-version Require main/dev, a clean tree and HEAD equal to fetched origin Semantic-release build hook uv lock && git add uv.lock && make build-package; build failure stops commit/tag/publication make release-assets Require the tag at HEAD and one wheel/sdist per PACKAGE_PROJECTS entry make release Run versioning, reuse valid artifacts or build missing ones, then upload sequentially

All workspace package versions equal the root version. Tags retain vX.Y.Z-rc.N spelling; Python artifacts use normalized X.Y.ZrcN filenames. CI retries may accept the exact tagged, single-parent chore(release): v<version> [skip ci] child of the tested source; newer application changes require validation. Git hooks are disabled only during semantic-release. With no new version or matching tag at HEAD, make release stops without uploading.

docs.title: Repository settings (once)
docs.text: Enable Actions release write permissions and configure Pages to deploy from gh-pages. Enable squash merging so PR titles determine versions. CI installs tools with --locked using install-tools, install-release or install-dev according to the job.

docs.title: After a release: sync main into dev
docs.text: Merge main back into dev after a stable release. Use the stable version/changelog as the base for the next candidate; see branch conventions.

docs.title: 6. Fork
docs.text: Create your repository with GitHub's "Use this template", then rename.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text:
What Where workspace name pyproject.toml: [project] name backend package backend/pyproject.toml name, folder backend/src/genai_template_backend/, imports in tests/ and frontend/ frontend package frontend/pyproject.toml name, folder frontend/src/genai_template_frontend/, imports in tests/ logger name bind(name=...) and its filter in both packages' settings modules run targets makefiles/run.mk (paths to app.py and main.py) containers Dockerfile*, docker-compose*.yml documentation README.md, AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md links to it), properdocs.yml (site_name), SECURITY.md, docs/ version and changelog semantic-release owns project.version and CHANGELOG.md; never edit them by hand

Then: uv lock, make install-dev, make check (it needs the integration prerequisites).

docs.title: Once on GitHub
docs.text:
1. Create main and dev, and protect them; use squash merges for pull requests. Allow release automation and the documented main → dev merge sync to push as needed.
  2. Workflow permissions "Read and write", and GitHub Pages from gh-pages (5. Release).
  3. Install the Renovate app on the repository.

docs.title: Stay in sync with upstream
docs.text:
Shared files: makefiles/, Makefile, scripts/emoji_commit_parser.py, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, .github/, docs/developer/.

git remote add upstream https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- makefiles/release.mk   # the files you want
git diff --staged                                     # review before committing

docs.title: Examples

Bases: LLMConnection

Embed text without inheriting generation behavior or schema detection.

Source code in backend/src/genai_template_backend/api/llm.py 
class EmbeddingLLMConfig(LLMConnection):
    """Embed text without inheriting generation behavior or schema detection."""

    def _connection_parameters(self):
        parameters = super()._connection_parameters()
        parameters["api_base"] = parameters.pop("base_url")
        return parameters

    def embed_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        response = litellm.embedding(**self._connection_parameters(), input=texts)
        return [item["embedding"] for item in response.data]

    def embed_text(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        return self.embed_texts([text])[0]

    async def a_embed_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        response = await litellm.aembedding(**self._connection_parameters(), input=texts)
        return [item["embedding"] for item in response.data]

    async def a_embed_text(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        return (await self.a_embed_texts([text]))[0]

    def get_model_name(self):
        return self.model_name

docs.title: InferenceLLMConfig
docs.text:
Bases: LLMConnection

Generate text or validated structured output without hiding provider errors.

Source code in backend/src/genai_template_backend/api/llm.py 
class InferenceLLMConfig(LLMConnection):
    """Generate text or validated structured output without hiding provider errors."""

    temperature: float | None = None
    seed: int | None = 1729
    max_tokens: int | None = None
    reasoning_effort: str | None = None

    @property
    def supports_response_schema(self) -> bool:
        return litellm.supports_response_schema(model=self.model_name)

    def _parameters(self, messages, **kwargs):
        parameters = {
            **self._connection_parameters(),
            "messages": messages,
            "timeout": settings.INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            "drop_params": True,
            "num_retries": 0,
        }
        for name in ("temperature", "seed", "max_tokens", "reasoning_effort"):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None:
                parameters[name] = value
        parameters.update(kwargs)
        return parameters

    def generate(self, prompt: str, schema=None, raw_response=False, **kwargs):
        return self.generate_from_messages(
            [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], schema, raw_response, **kwargs
        )

    async def a_generate(self, prompt: str, schema=None, raw_response=False, **kwargs):
        return await self.a_generate_from_messages(
            [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], schema, raw_response, **kwargs
        )

    @retry(
        wait=wait_fixed(settings.INFERENCE_RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS),
        stop=stop_after_attempt(settings.INFERENCE_MAX_ATTEMPTS),
        retry=(
            retry_if_exception_type(litellm.RateLimitError)
            | retry_if_exception_cause_type(litellm.RateLimitError)
        ),
        reraise=True,
    )
    def generate_from_messages(self, messages: list, schema=None, raw_response=False, **kwargs):
        parameters = self._parameters(messages, **kwargs)
        if schema and not self.supports_response_schema:
            client = instructor.from_litellm(litellm.completion, mode=instructor.Mode.JSON)
            output, response = client.chat.completions.create_with_completion(
                **parameters, response_model=schema, max_retries=1
            )
            return response if raw_response else output
        if schema:
            parameters["response_format"] = schema
        return _parse_response(litellm.completion(**parameters), schema, raw_response)

    @retry(
        wait=wait_fixed(settings.INFERENCE_RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS),
        stop=stop_after_attempt(settings.INFERENCE_MAX_ATTEMPTS),
        retry=(
            retry_if_exception_type(litellm.RateLimitError)
            | retry_if_exception_cause_type(litellm.RateLimitError)
        ),
        reraise=True,
    )
    async def a_generate_from_messages(
        self, messages: list, schema=None, raw_response=False, **kwargs
    ):
        parameters = self._parameters(messages, **kwargs)
        if schema and not self.supports_response_schema:
            client = instructor.from_litellm(litellm.acompletion, mode=instructor.Mode.JSON)
            output, response = await client.chat.completions.create_with_completion(
                **parameters, response_model=schema, max_retries=1
            )
            return response if raw_response else output
        if schema:
            parameters["response_format"] = schema
        return _parse_response(await litellm.acompletion(**parameters), schema, raw_response)

class LLMConnection(BaseModel):
    """Connection parameters shared by the two independent clients."""

    model_name: str
    base_url: str
    api_key: SecretStr
    api_version: str = "2025-02-01-preview"

    def _connection_parameters(self):
        return {
            "model": self.model_name,
            "base_url": self.base_url,
            "api_key": self.api_key.get_secret_value(),
            "api_version": self.api_version,
        }
